questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A somewhat level of academics alongside with opportunity for gaining cultural knowledge and share experiences in the legal field accros boarders. Also the acces to administrative help from the host university was crucial.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exceeded all expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything was send to my mail, and if I had questions everyone were nice to help, and easy to get in contact to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Directions and quick responses from the administrative team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were various "colleges" were you could rent a room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchens. Fridge in the room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very highly recommended. Great way to meet locals and ther exchange students. PLEAS do yourself the favour of connecting with the other local students in the buildings. It was an amazing insight in the life of italian students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Weekly cleaning of the room by staff was amazing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had to ask the administrative staff about the overall procedure and proces just to b e sure I understood, but everything was sent to you, so it was ver nice - just different from what I am used to.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: An excelark was uploaded on the university page (a link sent to your email with it too). Here you had to explore the classes you wanted to have, and then a couple of weeks later, maybe a week or two before departing, you could apply for them. However note that it is your own responsabilit not to have overlaps in the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administrative staff were always very helpfull and replied within a very short period of time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succefull. I accidentally applied for the wrong class, but it was possible to add and drop classes afterwards, so it was very easy to correct.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: PLease check the courseschedule for the classes you want. There is a big possibility that there are overlaps.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great, but different. And different is great, but I prefer the way we do it back home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think I had two BA classes and one MA. In all classes the level was a bit less than what I have been used too back home, but overall the classes and the courses were great, and still there was a lot to be gained, because you had another view and the material as well as the way to approach the subjects and teaching/learning experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Used to more interactive teaching, more case studies etc. Also oral exams at Luiss wuld just not be a thing at UCPH. It worked very well, just different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Roman Law (Istituzioni di dirrito Romano)
EU Law
Transnational criminal law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: EU law gave an amazing inside on how other countries view and value the vroad aspect of EU law at it was a great experience to see these things in a different light. Very informative.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You had to buy your own pans, pots and other kitchen ware to cook in the kitchen. This was appr. 500 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and transport is less expensive. Going out is more or less the same as back home, except for wine and local dishes. This is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont really know, I didnt participate in any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont really know, I didnt participate in any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A lot of sightseeing - the classics, but also all the museums and galleries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel italy, or explore Rome - the beaches are great when it gets hot rfom may-august.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very much, but I put a lot of effort into it also before arriving. I did however also get the feelign that the people who maybe didnt do as much adjusted quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn italian, and just be curious on them and the italian culture. Ask them to take you out to their favourite places.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Outside of the university, the basic level of english which the italians speak is very low....

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcome spirit that everyone has, the gentleman vibe to be found in italian male in all ages - the going-out-for-dinner-lunch-aperitivo culture is something you just have to love.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) learn a bit of italian, 2) dont stress about the administrative parts - everything is gonna happen, it is just a bit slow and last minute sometimes, 3) be serious about finding housing early on the proces, the campuses are recommended.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cant think of more than the above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Thinking back on the feeling I had when I landed. Not knowing anything, not having control, everything is new and different, and then comparing to now, when this citt feels like a home, and the school system is for some parts preferred to the danish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not knowing or really be able to check which room the exams were in. They would be put on a whiteboard on the day of the exam (I really didnt have that serious challenges hahah).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Thank you.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
